newsitem.title: UK: France may challenge Guinness merger - paper.
newsitem.headline: France may challenge Guinness merger - paper.

text.p: French authorities may question the planned merger between British drinks giants Guinness and Grand Metropolitan, the Independent reported on Monday.

The newspaper quoted trade sources as saying the French government would lobby the European Commission over the proposed merger because of concerns over global distribution of champagne falling into British hands.

Guinness holds a 34 percent stake in champagne company Moet Hennessy and has an exclusive, worldwide distribution deal with the company. French luxury goods group LVMH, headed by Bernard Arnault, owns the rest of the firm.
The Independent quoted a Guinness/Grand Met spokesman as saying champagne companies "remain absolutely under French control".
"French champagne producers will get even better distribution around the world (through GMG), which is what Mr Arnault wants anyway," the spokesman said.

The planned merger of Guinness and Grand Met, announced last Monday, would be the biggest in British corporate history and create the seventh largest food and drinks company in the world, to be called GMG Brands.
Arnault voted against the merger, expressing reservations about its rationale, said a Guinness/Grand Met statement last week.
